analysis.title: GS Basics Crowding Out. TSMC/Samsung. Cyclicals/RSP.
key_insights: Markets are on the back foot overnight. Nikkei is down about 1.4%, KOSPI is under more pressure and Taiwan is weaker despite very strong Samsung and TSMC numbers. Oil is back above $103, the US 10yr is around 5.3%, and the Fed minutes reinforce the prospect of another hike later this year.
Privorotsky argues that strong AI earnings are not enough to offset pressure from rates, energy and capital supply. The AI micro keeps accelerating while the macro backdrop gets harder.

Europe had a tough session yesterday. The short-lived oats/domestic rally reversed, and contagion spread beyond France into Italian and Greek sovereign risk. Pressure is further out the curve and the front end is relatively contained.
US cyclicals relative to equal-weight SPX are back near the lows of the year, and the broader European risk complex is struggling.

Capital crowding-out thesis: after the GFC, governments assumed abundant savings and low rates and expanded deficits and entitlement spending. Sovereign financing needs are now very large and the AI buildout adds unprecedented private capital demand. Reports of SpaceX seeking $40bn and Broadcom exploring more than $50bn of financing add to the point.

If scarce compute can generate 20-30% compounding IRRs, borrowers will pay high single-digit rates to build it. That strains consumers, small businesses and governments with balance sheets built for cheap capital. It may explain why real yields refuse to fall, since a large supply of high-quality private paper competes with sovereign duration.

Credit spreads remain relatively contained because all-in yields look attractive to investors. Extrapolating forward gives two outcomes: AI becomes largely self-financing from organic cash flow, making the next hyperscaler earnings particularly important, or capital is rationed elsewhere and weaker parts of the economy break. CCC spreads may already show the start of that.

Samsung reported operating profit of ₩107.4tn and TSMC Q3 sales are roughly 50% higher YoY and ahead of expectations. Both show very strong underlying demand. Smartphones within Samsung are squeezed by higher memory costs, and expectations may have been too high for the numbers to matter.

LG Electronics is flagged as a negative read-through. Earnings disappointed despite revenue growth, with logistics and input costs an increasing burden, which suggests the broader corporate picture outside AI is getting more complicated.

Oil is sharply higher overnight on renewed escalation risk. A tanker was struck off Qatar, showing attacks can extend beyond the Strait of Hormuz and block a return to normal, with implications for gas as well as oil. Freight is very expensive and physical crude is diverging from paper benchmarks.
Talks appear increasingly deadlocked. With the midterms approaching, Privorotsky is less convinced there is a credible off-ramp.
The 10yr auction went well yesterday, with a 2.77x cover and only 2.5% left with dealers. The 30yr auction is today. If all three auctions clear cleanly, rates technicals may be starting to heal.

Long-end vol remains elevated and the implied/realized vol premium has not normalized. Privorotsky wants to see these risk premia compress as evidence that intermediation capacity is returning, a prerequisite for more durable stability across asset classes.
AAII bull/bear sentiment is back to neutral, so the extreme negative sentiment tailwind is largely gone. Nasdaq has challenged its highs and positioning has chased the AI vertical.
Russell has underperformed NDX in 17 of the last 20 sessions. High oil and high real rates are a difficult combination for consumers, small businesses and leveraged balance sheets.

Privorotsky stays constructive on AI, saying almost every micro signal is green outside the cost of capital. He is increasingly unsure about the off-ramp for European sovereign risk and everything else in a high-rate world. Energy could have been the solver but is moving the wrong way.

tension_points.theme: AI capex vs cost of capital
tension_points.bull_case: Almost every micro signal is green. Samsung and TSMC show very strong demand, and if scarce compute earns 20-30% IRRs, AI can become self-financing from organic cash flow.
tension_points.bear_case: AI financing needs crowd out other borrowers, keep real yields high and strain consumers, small businesses and governments. CCC spreads may already show capital being rationed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The next hyperscaler earnings failing to show AI becoming self-financing, or weaker borrowers breaking as capital is rationed.
